## Skills
A skill is a set of instructions provided through a `SKILL.md` source. Below is the list of skills that can be used. Each entry includes a name, description, and source locator. `file` locators are on the host filesystem, `environment resource` locators are owned by an execution environment, `orchestrator resource` locators are opaque non-filesystem resources, and `custom resource` locators use their provider's access mechanism.
### Available skills
- imagegen: Generate or edit raster images when the task benefits from AI-created bitmap visuals such as photos, illustrations, textures, sprites, mockups, or transparent-background cutouts. Use when Codex should create a brand-new image, transform an existing image, or derive visual variants from references, and the output should be a bitmap asset rather than repo-native code or vector. Do not use when the task is better handled by editing existing SVG/vector/code-native assets, extending an established icon or logo system, or building the visual directly in HTML/CSS/canvas. # Reference-Aware Synthetic Retention

Add a `reference-aware-synthetic-retention` option, disabled by default, so users can prevent emitted Java from referring to a generated declaration its own output leaves out. When enabled, apply the new decision only to generated declarations that the active removal and reconstruction settings would otherwise omit: synthetic fields, methods, and member classes, and bridge methods. Declare each such member if the emitted Java of its file refers to it, and preserve its omission otherwise. Make that decision from the Java produced by the selected reconstruction settings. Where reconstruction consumes every reference to a generated member, that member remains omitted; where references remain, it is declared under the combination of reconstruction settings that produced them. When the option is disabled, output is unchanged.

A reference is a use of a member by emitted Java code that is itself part of the output. Omitted code refers to nothing, so a generated member reachable only from another omitted member is itself omitted. Text that is not code refers to nothing either, including comments and literal contents. One output file is decided as a whole: a member declared on the outermost class of a file and referred to only from a member class, local class, anonymous class, or lambda body within that same file is referred to.

Retention is decided per member. Declaring one generated member is no reason to declare its unreferenced siblings. Output that needs no generated declarations must not gain any, member for member.

The decision is deterministic for the same input: repeated runs and separate decompiler contexts agree on the same retained members, and a further round, over output that has been compiled again, agrees as well.

## Progress

Implemented `reference-aware-synthetic-retention`:

- Added `IFernflowerPreferences.REFERENCE_AWARE_SYNTHETIC_RETENTION`.
- Default is `"0"`; short name chosen as `ras`.
- Added per-output-root fixed-point retention in `ClassWriter`.
- Uses semantic `TextBuffer` tokens, so comments and literals do not count as references.
- Handles synthetic fields, synthetic/bridge methods, and synthetic member classes.
- Retains transitive dependencies while omitting members reachable only from omitted code.
- Shares analysis state with nested, anonymous, local, and lambda writers.
- Preserves existing behavior when disabled.
- Reconstruction/late-processing happens before reference analysis.

Added regression fixture:

- [TestReferenceAwareSynthetic.jasm](/app/testData/src/jasm/TestReferenceAwareSynthetic.jasm)
- [TestReferenceAwareSynthetic.dec](/app/testData/results/pkg/TestReferenceAwareSynthetic.dec)
- Registered in [SingleClassesTest.java](/app/test/org/jetbrains/java/decompiler/SingleClassesTest.java)

The fixture verifies:

- Referenced synthetic field is retained.
- Referenced synthetic method is retained.
- A synthetic field referenced only by that retained method is retained transitively.
- Unreferenced synthetic sibling remains omitted.
- Literal text mentioning a member does not retain it.

## Verification

Passed:

```text
./gradlew compileJava testClasses --no-daemon
./gradlew compileTestDataJasm --offline --no-daemon
./gradlew :test --offline --no-daemon --tests org.jetbrains.java.decompiler.SingleClassesTest
```

Manual checks also confirmed:

- Option-off output is unchanged.
- Reconstruction consuming a synthetic accessor leaves it omitted.
- Repeated option-enabled runs produce identical output.

A plain `./gradlew test --tests ...` invocation failed only because Gradle applied the filter to the `idea-not-null` subproject, which has no matching tests; root `:test` passed.

## Remaining work

Review and harden before final handoff:

- Run `git diff --check` and inspect the complete diff.
- Refactor the dense processor condition in `writeClassInternal` for readability.
- Remove unused `ClassNode` parameters from helper methods.
- Consider skipping `ClassNode.Type.LAMBDA` during candidate collection to avoid redundant parent-member scanning.
- Test option-enabled vs option-disabled output on annotation-heavy classes, since the fixed-point approach renders candidates more than once and annotation state may be mutable.
- Add focused bridge/member-class tests if practical.
- Decide whether synthetic constructors need explicit semantic reference tokens; current token detection covers fields, methods, and classes but not constructor calls directly.
- Run the broader root test suite if time permits.

steps.message:
## Handoff summary

Implemented `reference-aware-synthetic-retention`:

- Added preference constant and default `"0"` in [IFernflowerPreferences.java](/app/src/org/jetbrains/java/decompiler/main/extern/IFernflowerPreferences.java).
- Added fixed-point, per-output-root retention in [ClassWriter.java](/app/src/org/jetbrains/java/decompiler/main/ClassWriter.java).
- Uses semantic `TextBuffer` tokens, so comments/literals do not count.
- Candidate members are all potentially generated synthetic fields/methods, bridge methods, and synthetic member classes; after a baseline render, only declarations actually omitted by the normal renderer become candidates. This includes reconstruction-hidden methods.
- Nested/member/local/anonymous/lambda output shares retention state.
- Added annotation-state reset before each render because type-annotation duplicate suppression is mutable.
- Added fixture/test:
  - [TestReferenceAwareSynthetic.jasm](/app/testData/src/jasm/TestReferenceAwareSynthetic.jasm)
  - [TestReferenceAwareSynthetic.dec](/app/testData/results/pkg/TestReferenceAwareSynthetic.dec)
  - registration in [SingleClassesTest.java](/app/test/org/jetbrains/java/decompiler/SingleClassesTest.java)

Verified successfully:

- `./gradlew compileJava testClasses --no-daemon`
- `./gradlew compileJava --offline --no-daemon`
- `./gradlew :test --offline --no-daemon --tests org.jetbrains.java.decompiler.SingleClassesTest`
- Manual option-on/off comparisons for synthetic accessors, annotations, nested/lambda classes, records, and renaming.
- Type-annotation output initially differed across repeated renders; annotation reset fixed it and output now matches option-off output.

Current uncommitted files:

- `src/org/jetbrains/java/decompiler/main/ClassWriter.java`
- `src/org/jetbrains/java/decompiler/main/extern/IFernflowerPreferences.java`
- `test/org/jetbrains/java/decompiler/SingleClassesTest.java`
- two new fixture files above.

Remaining work:

1. Review the complete diff and run `git diff --check`.
2. Rerun the focused test after the latest annotation-reset change.
3. Decide whether to add constructor-use semantic tokens. Synthetic constructors are currently included as potential methods, but constructor calls are not represented by `MethodTextToken`; this was identified as a possible gap. A patch attempt for `NewExprent.java` failed and made no changes. If implemented, gate added tokens on the new option so option-off token/output behavior remains unchanged.
4. Add focused bridge/member-class coverage if practical.
5. Run broader root tests if time permits.

Important constraints: edit with `apply_patch`; preserve unrelated worktree changes; do not use destructive git commands.
